claims.text: The feedstock is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder suitable for laser-based additive manufacturing.
An appropriate intervention is in situ substrate or build-platform preheating at approximately 500–600°C.
Build-platform preheating elevates the base temperature and decreases the temperature differential between the substrate and melt pool.
Build-platform preheating reduces thermal gradients during solidification.
Reduced thermal gradients slow the cooling rate.
Reduced thermal gradients facilitate a more uniform elemental distribution.
Reduced thermal gradients facilitate more uniform grain formation.
Preheating reduces elemental segregation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating lowers residual stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Preheating reduces process-induced defect density in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The reductions in segregation, residual stress, and defects collectively improve mechanical integrity.
Preheated builds will have greater tensile strength than builds made without preheating.
Preheated builds will have greater ductility than builds made without preheating.
Laser-based additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi without preheating typically produces significant thermal gradients.
Laser-based additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi without preheating typically produces pronounced elemental segregation.
Laser-based additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi without preheating typically produces higher residual stresses and more defects.
The hypothesis applies under controlled-atmosphere laser processing with standardized energy input, scanning parameters, and uniform platform heating.
Changes in processing method, build geometry, or alloy system may change the outcome.
Existing evidence supports the predicted directional improvement from preheating.
